acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Crocodilians family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as River Crocodile, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Clamp Soldier archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Mature broad-snout crocodile with heavy dorsal scutes, mud-worn flanks, thick tail, and powerful forequarters.
Signature mechanic: Parallel-Groove Drag: the Crocodile's foreclaws cut two fixed grooves that define its backward towing path.
battlefieldDuty: Lunge a short distance, clamp one target, and drag backward without turning.
constructionDimensions: Mineral reinforcement follows dorsal scutes, skull roof, claw roots, and tail ridges while flexible hide and belly remain biological.
Mud banks crack, stones roll, and sediment compresses along the lunge or roll path without turning the animal into a statue.
counterplay: Sidestep the jaws or strike the planted forelegs during the backward drag. Affinity signal: A pale fault opens at the jaw hinge, planted foreleg, side-scute lock, or exposed belly after commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: Mineral armor that removes the vulnerable belly fault
identityInvariants: Every form retains a low four-legged crocodilian body, long tail, scuted back, belly fault, sensory pits, and a jaw-driven attack silhouette.
Tier escalation uses snout geometry, scute height, neck mobility, tail mass, scars, and waterline behavior rather than equipment or wings.
Eyes, wake direction, jaw angle, foreclaw grooves, tail curve, and exposed belly keep ambush and rotation counterplay readable.
telegraph: The jaw opens low and both foreclaws dig parallel grooves into the bank.
